newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chip stocks react negatively to budget.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chip stocks react negatively to budget.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks reacted negatively to the 1997 Budget announced on Friday.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks was down 4.18 points and the all-share EMAS index was down 0.62. The Second board index was up 631.36.

"It is no good. There is no corporate tax cut, and no increase in Employees Provident Fund contributions. It has been broadly disappointing for the stock market," said Irene Tan research manager at Vickers Ballas.
Volume was high with 310 million shares traded, valued at 2,465 million ringgit.
"The foreign funds did not have much time to react to the budget speech, but there was not much to excite the market anyway," said Myles MacMahon, head of sales at BZW in Singapore.

Analysts said incentives for information technology and multi-media related companies announced in the budget resulted in Dataprep moving up 3.10 ringgit to 16.90 and Lityan moving up 1.80 ringgit to 23.70 ringgit.
Tenaga was unchanged at 9.80 and Sime Darby was down 5 cents to 8.85, on profit taking after recent gains, contributing to the slide on the Composite Index, said MacMahon
